analysis:
All three changed files are test-only Swift files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Benchmark. The changes track an upstream mlx-swift-lm API update and have no production behavior. In BackendParityHarnessProbeTests.swift:16 and EngineV2BenchmarkMTPVerificationTests.swift (patch hunk near line 53) the stub LanguageModel.prepare signature changes from (windowSize:) to (state:, prefill:). This matches the new protocol requirement and only affects stub models. In EngineV2BenchmarkMTPAcceptanceTests.swift:36,52,53 and the verification test near line 48, Gemma4 configuration and draft-model types are now module-qualified as MLXLLM.*. That only resolves a name ambiguity or collision and does not change behavior.

I found no change to attestation, authorization, key handling, WebSocket protocol, prefix-cache storage or crypto (T-041 and its mitigations), or serving-authorization logic. The tests still pin the native KV precision policy, which is test coverage for T-041-adjacent engine behavior only. The test fixtures write temporary files under temp directories with random UUIDs and remove them on exit. They hold only synthetic tiny-model data and no secrets.

Remaining uncertainty is limited to the external dependency bump. The updated mlx-swift-lm API (state and prefill parameters) is not visible in the supplied evidence, and any production-side adaptation to it is not in this batch. Production code that calls the new prepare signature, for example one that could alter prefill or cache semantics, should be reviewed wherever the dependency pin changes. Nothing in these test files indicates a regression.
